newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African 1996 gold output tumbles to 40-year low.
newsitem.headline: S.African 1996 gold output tumbles to 40-year low.

text.p: South Africa's gold production dropped to a 40-year low of 494.62 tonnes in 1996 from 522.38 in 1995, the Chamber of Mines said on Monday.
The output in the world's largest gold producer last year was the lowest since 1956 when South Africa's gold mines produced 494.44 tonnes of the yellow metal.
South African gold output has been declining steadily with rising working costs and dwindling grades chipping away at production in the country.
The chamber noted 1996 gold output was 5.3 percent lower than the previous year.

"It is estimated that the decline in production of 27.8 tonnes is equivalent to a loss of revenue to the industry and foreign exchange to South Africa to the order of 1.5 billion rand ($340 million)," the chamber said.
It said reasons for the drop in production included workplace disruptions, consolidation in the industry, escalating costs and a focus on quality mining at the expense of tonnage.
